unit.unitOverview: Say the seven days of the week. Put things in order: first to tenth. Say the day and time: on Monday, in the morning. Say: I am with a friend. It is for you. Last, check Units 0 to 6.
unit.learningPath:
The lesson: listen and repeat.
Words: listen, look and say. 26 words.
Patterns: 3 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read 3 short texts out loud.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about your week. Made-up is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. Five are on Units 0 to 5.

visual.lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 6.
In this unit, you say the day and the time.
Units 0 to 6 are Stage 1.
This is the last unit of Stage 1.
Listen. A week has seven days.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.
Thursday, Friday.
Saturday, Sunday.
Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
A day starts with a capital letter: Monday.
Wednesday: say Wenz-day.
Thursday: start with th, like three.
Now order words. Listen and repeat.
First, second, third.
Fourth, fifth, sixth.
Seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth.
Monday is the first day of the week.
Sunday is the seventh day.
First, second and third are new words.
Four and th: fourth. Six and th: sixth.
Five changes: fifth. Nine changes: ninth.
Now say the day with on.
On Monday. On Friday. On Sunday.
Say the part of the day with in.
In the morning. In the afternoon. In the evening.
On Saturday, I am in the park.
In the evening, I like cooking.
A day and a part of the day: on Monday morning.
What time is it?
It is eight o'clock.
It is three o'clock in the afternoon.
Now with and for.
With: a person is next to you.
I am walking with a friend.
For: a thing is going to a person.
This card is for my sister. It is her card now.
Last, the Stage 1 check.
The quiz has questions on Units 0 to 5, too.
Practice 6 and Writing 4 check Stage 1.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

readings.passageScript:
Hello! My name is Ivan. I am 20.
On Monday and Tuesday, I am at work.
On Wednesday evening, I am at school. It is an English school.
On Saturday, I like playing football with my brother.
On Sunday morning, I like cooking for my family.
Sunday is my favourite day of the week.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 3; Grade 1 Unit 10
grammar.title: First to tenth
grammar.explanation:
Say the order of things.
First is number 1. Second is number 2.
First, second and third are new words.
From fourth, add th to the number.
Say the before it: the first day.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
1st — first
2nd — second
3rd — third
4th — fourth
5th — fifth
6th — sixth
7th — seventh
8th — eighth
9th — ninth
10th — tenth

Add th: four, fourth. six, sixth. ten, tenth.
Three change:
five — fifth
eight — eighth (one t)
nine — ninth (no e)

Monday is the first day of the week.
The shop is on the second floor.
grammar.workedExample:
Write 5th as a word.
1. 5th is number 5.
2. 5 is five.
3. Five changes: fif.
4. Add th: fifth.
5. Check the list: 5th, fifth. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to add th to five and nine.
No: fiveth, nineth.
Yes: fifth, ninth.
Eight has one t: eighth.
grammar.memoryTip: Say the: the first day, the second floor.
grammar.practice:
Write the word.
1. 1st
2. 3rd
3. 2nd
4. 5th
5. 9th
6. 8th
7. Thursday is the ___ day of the week.
8. Sunday is the ___ day of the week.
grammar.answerKey:
1. first  2. third  3. second  4. fifth  5. ninth  6. eighth  7. fourth  8. seventh
Wrong on 4? Five changes: fifth, not fiveth.
Wrong on 5? Nine loses its e: ninth, not nineth.
Wrong on 7 or 8? Count from Monday: first.

grammar.title: On Monday, in the morning
grammar.explanation:
Say the day and the time.
Use on with a day: on Monday.
Use in with a part of the day: in the morning.
A day and a part of the day: on Monday morning.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
on — a day
on Monday
on Friday
on Saturday and Sunday

in the — a part of the day
in the morning
in the afternoon
in the evening

a day and a part of the day — on
on Monday morning
on Friday night

On Sunday, I am in the park.
I am in the park on Sunday.

It is two o'clock in the afternoon.
grammar.workedExample:
I am at work ___ Tuesday.
1. Tuesday is a day.
2. A day goes with on.
3. Write: I am at work on Tuesday.
4. Check: a day, so on. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to use in with a day.
No: in Monday.
Yes: on Monday.
No: on the morning.
Yes: in the morning.
grammar.memoryTip: A day: on. Morning, afternoon, evening: in the.
grammar.practice:
Write on or in.
1. The shop is closed ___ Sunday.
2. I like walking ___ the evening.
3. ___ the morning, I am at school or at work.
4. I can play football ___ Saturday.
5. It is four o'clock ___ the afternoon.
6. My sister is working ___ Tuesday.
7. I am cooking ___ Friday evening.
grammar.answerKey:
1. on  2. in  3. In  4. on  5. in  6. on  7. on
Wrong on 7? Friday evening has a day in it. A day: on.
Number 3 starts the line, so write In with a capital.

grammar.title: With a friend, for my sister
grammar.explanation:
With: a person is next to you.
I am walking with Sam.
For: a thing is going to a person.
This cup is for Sam. It is his cup now.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
with — a person next to you
I am walking with a friend.
She is playing football with her brother.
I like cooking with my mother.

for — a thing going to a person
This card is for my sister.
I have got a pen for you.
The photo is for my grandmother.

Who are you with? I am with my cousin.
Who is it for? It is for my aunt.
grammar.workedExample:
This bag is ___ my mother. It is her bag now.
1. The bag is going to my mother.
2. It is her bag now.
3. A thing going to a person: for.
4. Write: This bag is for my mother.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to say for in place of with.
No: I am walking for my friend.
Yes: I am walking with my friend.
Is the person next to you? Use with.
grammar.memoryTip: With: next to you. For: it is going to the person.
grammar.practice:
Write with or for.
1. This card is ___ my sister. It is her card now.
2. I am walking ___ a friend. We are talking.
3. I have got a pen ___ you. Here it is.
4. Mia and her brother are in the park. Mia is playing ___ her brother.
5. The cup is ___ my grandmother. It is her cup now.
6. On Sunday, I am in the park ___ my cousin.
grammar.answerKey:
1. for  2. with  3. for  4. with  5. for  6. with
Wrong on 2, 4 or 6? The person is next to you, so with.
Wrong on 1, 3 or 5? The thing is going to the person, so for.

activities.title: Practice 2 — The missing day
activities.instructionsAndItems:

1. Monday, ___, Wednesday
2. Tuesday, ___, Thursday
3. ___, Sunday, Monday
4. Sunday, ___, Tuesday
5. Wednesday, Thursday, ___

activities.answerSummary:

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a checklist the learner can see. If you are helping, let the key do the correcting: point to the line, and let the learner find the difference themselves.

teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 3; Grade 1 Unit 10
teacherNotes.note: This is the last unit of Stage 1 (Units 0 to 6). Quiz items 8 to 12 revisit Units 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5; Practice 6 has one line from each unit with the unit named in brackets; Writing 4 and the assignment ask for one pattern from each unit in six lines. A learner who misses two or more of the recap items should go back to the unit named in the key before Stage 2, not repeat this one.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 3; Grade 1 Unit 10
teacherNotes.note: Three slips to listen for. In with a day (in Monday), because in was just learned for places and for the morning. Spelling the order words by adding th to every number (fiveth, nineth, eightth). And Tuesday and Thursday mixed up, since both start with T and are said fast. The keys name all three, so the learner can find them without being told.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 3; Grade 1 Unit 10
teacherNotes.note: At for time is Unit 11 (at six o'clock, at night) and at the weekend is Unit 16, so the unit avoids them: night appears as on Friday night, and the weekend as a noun. If a learner says in the night, let it go for now. Sentences such as On Saturday, I am playing football use Unit 5's -ing for a plan; present simple for routines is Unit 14, and months and dates like the 21st are Units 9 and 10.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 3; Grade 1 Unit 10
teacherNotes.note: The unit follows the common English calendar: Monday is the first day and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday. Many learners live with a different working week. That is a fact about their calendar, not an error in their English: in their own writing, accept the days that are true for them, as long as the day names and on are right.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: in — Morning, afternoon, evening: in the. On is for a day. At goes with a place. For is for a thing going to a person.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: for — The card is going to my sister, so for. With is for a person next to you. On and in are for days and parts of the day.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: with — My brother and I are in the park, so with. For is for a thing going to a person. On and in are for days and parts of the day.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: It is five o'clock. — What time asks for a number and o'clock. Monday is a day. The fifth is an order word. I am five is an age.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Saturday — Sun and Saturday start with the s sound. Thursday starts with th, like three. Monday starts with m. Wednesday starts with w.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Their — Their goes before a thing: their bag. They is for the people, not the bag. There is a place. His is for one man.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: a red bag — The colour goes before the thing: a red bag. Red has no -s. A goes first.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: cooking — Like and -ing: I like cooking. Cook and cooks have no -ing. To cooking is not right.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: is running — Now: am, is or are and -ing. Tomas is one man, so is. Are is for you, we and they. Running needs is. Run has no -ing.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
